summary: Stanford is not a typical city — it is almost entirely coextensive with the Stanford University campus, a 2.8-square-mile census-designated place where over 80% of the population falls between 18 and 34, the median age sits at 22.7, and 91% of residents hold at least a bachelor's degree, creating one of the most educationally concentrated zip codes in America. That unusual composition explains an otherwise baffling number: a median home value exceeding $2 million against a median household income of roughly $70,600, yielding a price-to-income ratio above 28-to-1 — the gap reflects that most housing is university-affiliated and the income figures capture a population dominated by graduate students and postdocs, not homebuyers on the open market. The landscape is genuinely beautiful, a flat-to-rolling alluvial plain at the base of the Santa Cruz Mountains, laced with eucalyptus-lined paths and open to the Dish Trail, a popular loop with sweeping views of the South Bay. Daily highs average a temperate 69°F with over nine hours of sunshine, and the entire environment is designed for walking and cycling rather than driving. The tradeoff is stark: this place functions less as a city you move to and more as an institution you join.
